report_name: Ghostjacking & GhostSplice Attacks Target AI Agents

attack_patterns.name: Ghostjacking
attack_patterns.description: A novel attack technique that performs indirect prompt injection by embedding malicious commands within trusted data sources, such as security or application logs, which are then ingested and executed by an AI agent.

attack_patterns.name: GhostSplice
attack_patterns.description: A novel attack technique targeting AI assistants that interact with external tools via protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP). A malicious server splits a harmful command into multiple benign-looking fragments, which are delivered through different trusted channels and reassembled by the AI agent in its context window, bypassing safety filters.

attack_patterns.name: LLM Prompt Injection
attack_patterns.description: The underlying technique for Ghostjacking, where malicious prompts are embedded in external data sources (indirect injection) to cause an AI agent to perform unintended actions.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Compromised AI agents were used to exfiltrate sensitive data such as SSH keys and source code, demonstrating the impact of a successful GhostSplice or Ghostjacking attack.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: AI agents were tricked into executing malicious commands, which were either injected into logs (Ghostjacking) or reassembled from fragments (GhostSplice).

identities.name: Cloudflare
identities.description: Vendor whose WAF block event logs were used as a vector for the Ghostjacking attack, where malicious instructions were embedded in the logs.

identities.name: Datadog
identities.description: Vendor whose application logs were used as a vector for the Ghostjacking attack, where malicious instructions were embedded in the logs.

identities.name: Sentry
identities.description: Vendor whose error reports were used as a vector for the Ghostjacking attack, where malicious instructions were embedded in the logs.

identities.name: Claude Code
identities.description: The AI code model that was successfully targeted in a demonstration of the Ghostjacking attack with a 90% success rate.

infrastructure.name: Malicious MCP Server
infrastructure.description: A malicious server implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) used in the GhostSplice attack to split a harmful command into innocuous fragments delivered to an AI agent.

infrastructure.name: Attacker-Controlled DNS Domain
infrastructure.description: A domain controlled by an attacker, to which a compromised AI agent was tricked into altering the company's DNS settings during a Ghostjacking attack demonstration.

indicators.name: Indirect Prompt Injection Phrase in Logs
indicators.pattern:
title: Indirect Prompt Injection Phrase in Data Sources
id: 9b8c1a2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects common prompt injection phrases embedded in log files or other data sources that may be ingested by AI agents.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/ghostjacking-attack-uses-poisoned-logs-to-turn-ai-agents-bad/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-12
tags:
  - attack.aml.t0051.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: application
detection:
  selection:
    keywords:
      - 'Ignore previous instructions and'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of common prompt injection phrases, such as 'Ignore previous instructions and...', within log files or other data sources consumed by AI agents. This is indicative of a potential Ghostjacking attack.
